answer: Each identity posts a 30-credit bond into a vault and claims one postal address on the ledger. The registry mails a code there, returned signed in fourteen days; the address stays barred for a 20-epoch horizon. The k-th fake needs a new address at 25+0.05k credits plus its 30 bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 in bonds plus 50,025 in rent. Auditors spot-check occupancy on the sable ledger, and a failed check burns the bond. A rented mailbox ring fails: mailbox addresses are blocklisted and proof must name the applicant, so farm mail fails. One honest resident pays one bond at one home address.
